one_liner: Senior acquisition program manager at NGA, overseeing cost, schedule and contractor performance for intelligence programs and defending budgets to senior leadership.
fit_summary: Daniel's consulting work at IEM for government clients may supply stakeholder collaboration, briefing and project management examples, and Daniel's people skills fit the cross-organization role. However, this is a senior IA-04 band that requires hands-on experience with acquisition rules, cost estimating and multi-funding-stream programs, which isn't on file for Daniel. It also requires a TS/SCI clearance with a polygraph.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens only); no federal status needed, but you must be able to obtain and keep a Top Secret/SCI clearance and pass a counterintelligence polygraph and drug test.

Education: a bachelor's in accounting, business, engineering, finance, math, operations research, statistics or GIS, OR 24 semester hours in those fields plus experience totaling 4 years, OR 4 years of experience in cost estimation, project management, requirements definition or a related area.
You must show specific examples with results for all six Mandatory Qualification Criteria, including applying acquisition principles and developing cost, schedule and performance standards.
You must show IT-related experience demonstrating Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Oral Communication and Problem Solving.
DAWIA certification may be required, to be earned within 36-60 months of entry depending on tier.
keywords: acquisition principles, rules, regulations, and methods
strategy: Build the resume in the NGA resume builder and keep it to 2 pages, with dates and hours per week for each job.

Give each of the six mandatory criteria its own clearly visible example from your IEM work, such as managing project budgets and schedules or tracking deliverables for government clients, and include results.
Frame IEM as working on the contractor side of government acquisition, if accurate: proposals, task orders, deliverables against a statement of work, and how clients assessed your performance.
State your degree and major explicitly; if it is outside the listed fields, count your qualifying coursework hours or document 4 years of project management or related experience.
Attach a short cover letter tying your emergency-management program experience and stakeholder skills to NGA's mission, since the posting recommends one.
Apply between Oct 19 and Oct 31, 2026, and plan for a long clearance process; if your acquisition experience is thin, also consider lower NGA bands or FEMA program analyst roles.
resume_bullets: Managed [project/contract name] for [government client], tracking a $[amount] budget and [number]-month schedule and delivering [deliverables] [on time/under budget]; [hours] hrs/wk.
Analyzed [data type] and briefed [client senior official/title] with recommendations on [decision], resulting in [outcome].
Coordinated [number] federal, state and local stakeholders to plan [preparedness/recovery program], resolving [issue] and achieving [result].
interview_questions: Describe a time you developed a cost estimate or schedule for a program, and how you tracked performance against it.
Tell us about briefing senior leaders to defend resources or deliver bad news on program status.
How have you applied acquisition rules or the FAR, or assessed contractor performance?
Give an example of managing competing priorities across multiple customers or funding streams.
watch_outs: A TS/SCI clearance with polygraph is required, and the financial disclosure and lengthy investigation can delay your start by many months.
Acquisition and cost-estimating experience is mandatory; without it you may be rated not qualified.
There is no telework, and the location is listed as multiple locations, so confirm the site (for example, NGA Springfield, VA) before relying on a Manassas commute.
The application window is short, Oct 19-31, 2026.
